rationale: Both are correct and well commented. A defines its errors once as package-level sentinels, which is idiomatic and easier to compare against. It has a single gameOver predicate that both Roll and Score use, and its Score loop handles all ten frames the same way without a special branch. B splits tenth-frame handling into small, readable helpers (validateTenthRoll, tenthFrameComplete, advanceFrame), which reads more explicitly. However, B builds the same error strings with errors.New in several places, duplicates the append/increment logic across two paths, and puts an awkward frame<9 branch inside the Score loop. A's cumulative-pins trick for the tenth-frame third roll (pinsInFrame < 20) is a little terse, but it is correct and commented. On balance A is the cleaner, more cohesive design.
